# Shared Python environment: Python 3.12 (deadsnakes PPA) on Ubuntu 22.04 in WSL2.
# Created by env/setup_python_env.sh; exact resolved versions are written to
# env/requirements-lock.txt after installation.
#
# Source of truth for the integration-critical pins below: the official ns-3.48
# guide doc/installation/source/sionna-rt.rst ("Instructions are for Python 3.12
# because that is the version we have tested"), which installs
#   sionna==1.2.0  sionna-rt==1.2.0  pybind11==2.11.1  cppyy==3.5.0
# and configures ns-3 with --enable-python-bindings.
#
# Why ONE environment: ns-3's Sionna RT channel model (src/spectrum) and the
# 5G-LENA example cttc-nr-demo-sionna-rt are only built if cppyy, sionna.rt and
# pybind11 are importable by the Python seen at configure time, and at run time
# the C++ code imports sionna.rt and numpy from that same Python.

# --- ns-3 / Sionna integration (versions as tested by ns-3) -----------------
# Ray tracing; pulls mitsuba==3.7.1, drjit==1.2.0. Same version is used for
# standalone Python ray tracing, so both simulation levels share one engine.
sionna-rt==1.2.0
pybind11==2.11.1
cppyy==3.5.0
# ns-3's tested set has numpy<2.0 (pinned by sionna==1.2.0), and pybind11 2.11
# predates NumPy 2 support. The full 'sionna' package (TensorFlow) is NOT
# installed: the ns-3 C++ code imports only sionna.rt and numpy (verified in
# src/spectrum/model/sionna-rt-channel-model.cc).
numpy==1.26.4

# --- Build tool for ns-3 -------------------------------------------------------
# ns-3.48 requires CMake >= 3.25 (cmake_minimum_required 3.25..3.25); Ubuntu
# 22.04 ships 3.22.1. The venv copy takes precedence on PATH when active.
# Pinned to the final 3.x release (avoids CMake 4 policy changes).
cmake==3.31.10

# --- Optimization benchmarks (exact MILP / CP-SAT) ----------------------------
highspy==1.15.1
# 9.14.6206 is the newest OR-Tools allowing numpy 1.x (9.15 requires numpy>=2.0.2,
# which conflicts with the ns-3 tested numpy 1.26.4 above).
ortools==9.14.6206

# --- Analysis and testing (resolved by pip; see lock file) --------------------
scipy
pandas
matplotlib
pytest
